knowledge_point.title: Cases When the Transformation Is Inferred From the Domain

question.:question/problem:
Use a change of variables to evaluate the double integral

$$
\iint_D x + y\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y
$$

where $D=\{(x,y):0\le x\le 4,\quad 0\le x + y\le 2\}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane to our region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dxdy={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v),y(u,v))\,|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\text{ }dudv
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

To compute the required integral, we proceed as follows:

**Step 1**: Find a suitable change of variables.

The inequalities that define the region $D,$

$$
0\le x\le 4,\quad 0\le x + y\le 2,
$$

suggest that we use the change of variables

$$
u=x\,\text{and}\,v=x + y.
$$

This change of variables gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}u(x,y) \\ v(x,y)\end{bmatrix}.
$$

**Step 2**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$

Our domain in the $uv$-plane is

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v):0\le u\le 4,\,0\le v\le 2\}.
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v)}{\partial(x,y)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}&\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}\\\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}&\frac{\partial v}{\partial y}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left|\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0\\1 & 1\end{bmatrix}\right|\\&=1.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 4**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v)}{\partial(x,y)}\right)^{-1}=1=1.
$$

Note that $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\ne0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

Solving the transformation equations gives $x=u,\ y=- u + v$, so the transformation is one-to-one on this domain.

**Step 5**: Perform the change of variables, and evaluate the integral:

Performing the change of variables, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_D x + y\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y & =\iint_\Delta v\left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|\,\mathrm{d}u\,\mathrm{d}v \\ & =\iint_\Delta \left(v\right)\cdot \left(1\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\,\mathrm{d}v \\ & =1\int_{0}^{2} [\int_{0}^{4} v\,\mathrm{d}u]\,\mathrm{d}v \\ & =1\int_{0}^{2} v[\int_{0}^{4} 1\,\mathrm{d}u]\,\mathrm{d}v \\ & =1\int_{0}^{2} v\left[u\right]_{0}^{4}\,\mathrm{d}v \\ & =1\int_{0}^{2} v\left(\left(4\right)-(\left(0\right))\right)\,\mathrm{d}v \\ & =\left(1\right)\cdot \left(4\right)\int_{0}^{2} v\,\mathrm{d}v \\ & =\left(1\right)\cdot \left(4\right)\left[\frac{v^{2}}{2}\right]_{0}^{2} \\ & =\left(1\right)\cdot \left(4\right)\left(\left(2\right)-(\left(0\right))\right) \\ & =\left(1\right)\cdot \left(4\right)\cdot \left(2\right) \\ & =8\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Use a change of variables to evaluate the double integral

$$
\iint_D e^{x^{2} + x + 4 y}\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y
$$

where $D=\{(x,y):1\le x\le 4,\quad 1\le x^{2} + 4 y\le 3\}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane to our region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dxdy={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v),y(u,v))\,|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\text{ }dudv
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

To compute the required integral, we proceed as follows:

**Step 1**: Find a suitable change of variables.

The inequalities that define the region $D,$

$$
1\le x\le 4,\quad 1\le x^{2} + 4 y\le 3,
$$

suggest that we use the change of variables

$$
u=x\,\text{and}\,v=x^{2} + 4 y.
$$

This change of variables gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}u(x,y) \\ v(x,y)\end{bmatrix}.
$$

**Step 2**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$

Our domain in the $uv$-plane is

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v):1\le u\le 4,\,1\le v\le 3\}.
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v)}{\partial(x,y)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}&\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}\\\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}&\frac{\partial v}{\partial y}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left|\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0\\2 x & 4\end{bmatrix}\right|\\&=4.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 4**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v)}{\partial(x,y)}\right)^{-1}=\frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

Note that $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\ne0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

Solving the transformation equations gives $x=u,\ y=- \frac{u^{2}}{4} + \frac{v}{4}$, so the transformation is one-to-one on this domain.

**Step 5**: Perform the change of variables, and evaluate the integral:

Performing the change of variables, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_D e^{x^{2} + x + 4 y}\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y & =\iint_D e^{x+(x^{2} + 4 y)}\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y \\ & =\iint_\Delta e^{u + v}\left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|\,\mathrm{d}u\,\mathrm{d}v \\ & =\iint_\Delta \left(e^{u + v}\right)\cdot \left(\frac{1}{4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\,\mathrm{d}v \\ & =\frac{1}{4}\int_{1}^{4} [\int_{1}^{3} e^{u} e^{v}\,\mathrm{d}v]\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & =\frac{1}{4}\int_{1}^{4} \left(e^{u}\right)[\int_{1}^{3} e^{v}\,\mathrm{d}v]\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & =\frac{1}{4}\int_{1}^{4} \left(e^{u}\right)\left[e^{v}\right]_{1}^{3}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & =\frac{1}{4}\int_{1}^{4} \left(e^{u}\right)\left(\left(e^{3}\right)-(\left(e\right))\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & =\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)\cdot \left(e^{3} - e\right)\int_{1}^{4} e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & =\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)\cdot \left(e^{3} - e\right)\left[e^{u}\right]_{1}^{4} \\ & =\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)\cdot \left(e^{3} - e\right)\left(\left(e^{4}\right)-(\left(e\right))\right) \\ & =\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)\cdot \left(e^{4} - e\right)\cdot \left(e^{3} - e\right) \\ & =\frac{e^{2}}{4} - \frac{e^{4}}{4} - \frac{e^{5}}{4} + \frac{e^{7}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Use a change of variables to evaluate the double integral

$$
\iint_D e^{x^{2} + x + y}\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y
$$

where $D=\{(x,y):0\le x\le 5,\quad 0\le x^{2} + y\le 3\}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane to our region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dxdy={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v),y(u,v))\,|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\text{ }dudv
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

To compute the required integral, we proceed as follows:

**Step 1**: Find a suitable change of variables.

The inequalities that define the region $D,$

$$
0\le x\le 5,\quad 0\le x^{2} + y\le 3,
$$

suggest that we use the change of variables

$$
u=x\,\text{and}\,v=x^{2} + y.
$$

This change of variables gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}u(x,y) \\ v(x,y)\end{bmatrix}.
$$

**Step 2**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$

Our domain in the $uv$-plane is

$$
\Delta=\{(u,v):0\le u\le 5,\,0\le v\le 3\}.
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v)}{\partial(x,y)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}&\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}\\\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}&\frac{\partial v}{\partial y}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left|\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0\\2 x & 1\end{bmatrix}\right|\\&=1.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 4**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v)}{\partial(x,y)}\right)^{-1}=1=1.
$$

Note that $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\ne0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

Solving the transformation equations gives $x=u,\ y=- u^{2} + v$, so the transformation is one-to-one on this domain.

**Step 5**: Perform the change of variables, and evaluate the integral:

Performing the change of variables, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_D e^{x^{2} + x + y}\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y & =\iint_D e^{x+(x^{2} + y)}\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y \\ & =\iint_\Delta e^{u + v}\left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|\,\mathrm{d}u\,\mathrm{d}v \\ & =\iint_\Delta \left(e^{u + v}\right)\cdot \left(1\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\,\mathrm{d}v \\ & =1\int_{0}^{5} [\int_{0}^{3} e^{u} e^{v}\,\mathrm{d}v]\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & =1\int_{0}^{5} \left(e^{u}\right)[\int_{0}^{3} e^{v}\,\mathrm{d}v]\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & =1\int_{0}^{5} \left(e^{u}\right)\left[e^{v}\right]_{0}^{3}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & =1\int_{0}^{5} \left(e^{u}\right)\left(\left(e^{3}\right)-(\left(1\right))\right)\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & =\left(1\right)\cdot \left(e^{3} - 1\right)\int_{0}^{5} e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & =\left(1\right)\cdot \left(e^{3} - 1\right)\left[e^{u}\right]_{0}^{5} \\ & =\left(1\right)\cdot \left(e^{3} - 1\right)\left(\left(e^{5}\right)-(\left(1\right))\right) \\ & =\left(1\right)\cdot \left(e^{5} - 1\right)\cdot \left(e^{3} - 1\right) \\ & =- e^{3} - e^{5} + e^{8} + 1\end{aligned}
$$
